Essay p643.text: Thus, both the unifying move which brings landscape as such into being, and the mood that a landscape projects at us and through which we comprehend it, are merely the result of a subsequent dismantling of one and the same psychic act.

transcription.original_text: Thus, both the unifying move which brings landscape as such into being, and the mood that a landscape projects at us and through which we comprehend it, are merely the result of a subsequent dismantling of one and the same psychic act.

Essay p643.alignment: One complete English sentence corresponds to the original sentence: the formation of landscape and the mood through which it is grasped are subsequent analyses of a single psychic act.

Personally read German printed p. 643 and publisher preview English p. 225; this complete sentence and punctuation match the image. The translation preserves the shared subsequent analysis of a single psychic act, though unifying move renders the German Einheit more dynamically. Josef Bleicher is identified as translator in Simmel Studies bibliography and the anthology source.
